item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 281730
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fausto, located in the Central Pacific several hundred miles
east-northeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Genevieve,
located several hundred miles southwest of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Public Advisory Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 282036
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
200 PM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE CONTINUES TO SLOWLY WEAKEN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.0N 116.9W
ABOUT 565 MI...910 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...955 MB...28.20 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was 
located near latitude 18.0 North, longitude 116.9 West. Genevieve is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this 
general motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 120 mph (195 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Genevieve is a category 3 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.  Steady weakening is forecast 
over the next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 955 mb (28.20 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula.
These swells are likely to persist for a few more days, and could
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams/Beven

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 282037
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
200 PM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026
 
Recent satellite imagery shows dry air entrainment along the 
northern and western side of the eye, resulting in some erosion of 
the structure of Genevieve. An earlier SSMIS pass continued to show 
a minor amount of northerly wind shear. Small fluctuations in 
strength have likely occurred this morning and afternoon, as 
evidenced by changes in the appearance of the eye and warming, 
followed by cooling, cloud top temperatures in the eyewall. The 
latest subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB was 5.5/102 
kt, while the objective estimates range from 97-107 kt. Given these 
estimates and taking into account the evolving satellite 
presentation, the initial intensity has been set at 105 kt.
 
Genevieve is moving west-northwestward at around 8 kt along the 
southwestern periphery of a ridge centered over the central and 
southern United States. A slightly faster forward speed is 
anticipated during the latter half of the week as the ridge expands 
westward and a strengthening upper-level low approaches the 
northwestern U.S. The track guidance shifted slightly farther south 
on this forecast cycle, and the official forecast has followed suit, 
and lies in the middle of the guidance envelope, close to HCCA. By 
late this weekend, guidance begins to diverge, and the forecast is 
positioned between the previous forecast track and HCCA.

After small fluctuations in strength today, Genevieve will gradually 
weaken as it moves over progressively cooler sea-surface 
temperatures and into a drier mid-level environment. On Thursday, 
Genevieve is forecast to move north of 20N, where SSTs fall below 26 
C, resulting in faster rate of weakening through the weekend. The 
latest NHC official intensity forecast shows Genevieve weakening to 
a tropical storm in a couple of days, and transitioning to a 
post-tropical cyclone this weekend.
